summary: Esho Yamaguchi (b. 1918) studied at Kyoto University and worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University and Osaka University, where he was a professor (attested 1980–1984).

Eshō Mikogami (1935–2018) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who founded Indogaku Chibettogaku Kenkyū. He served as president of the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies (1997) and was a professor until 2003 and later professor emeritus at Ryukoku University.

Ester Bianchi (b. 1971) studied under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, completing her PhD at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE (~1999–2003). A specialist in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she held posts at Florence and Perugia (~2007).

Etsuaki Teraishi worked in Indology and philosophy. Teraishi held an assistant professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and a special researcher post at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler (~1880–1886). From around 1886 to 1903, he served as an epigraphist for the Government of Madras, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Government of India.

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga (~1873–1876). In 1881, he was a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) studied under August Schleicher (~1862–1864) and worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from around 1869 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held research positions at the University of Pennsylvania (~1908–1913) and Johns Hopkins (~1913–1917), followed by a lectureship in Pāli at Yale (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang studied under John M. Rosenfield and Wu Hung, specializing in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a post at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) before becoming professor of Asian art at Harvard University (~1997).

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) studied (~1919–1926) and taught (~1928–1939) at Lviv University. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he later held posts at Nicolaus Copernicus University (~1946–1953) and the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971), heading Indology.

Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy and worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique (1826, 1832) and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1828–1832) and later under Eugène Burnouf (~1832–1838).

Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1927–1935) and the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies (~1930–1935).

Eun-su Cho (b. 1958) earned her PhD under Padmanabh S. Jaini at the University of California, Berkeley. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, she served as an assistant professor at Michigan until 2004, when she joined Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choi (b. 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Korea University. She held an HK professor post at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eva K. Neumaier (b. 1937) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Her career includes serving as professor and chair of East Asian Studies at the University of Alberta and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Calgary (attested 2006).
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay (b. 1937) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held a post at the University of Calgary.

Evan Thompson (b. 1962) studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His philosophy posts include Concordia, York University (2002–2005), Toronto (2005), and the University of British Columbia (2013).

Eviatar Shulman (b. 1973) studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1997–2008), working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He held posts there starting in 2009, including as a Mandel postdoctoral fellow at the Scholion center (attested 2015).

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Supervised by Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, he earned a PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.
